system.biography:
This enormous boar has a black-bristled hide marked by hundreds of old scars. Its eyes are wild and bloodshot, and its tusks are more than three feet long, gleaming like polished ivory and sharper than many swords.

Combat

A razor boar attacks intruders on its territory without provocation or warning. If attacking more than one target, it often attempts to trample it's opponents. The creature is swift for its size, and the thickness of it's hide allows it to shrug off many blows. Razor boars, with their fast healing, have been known to recover from seemingly mortal wounds, track down their attackers using their scent ability, and exact revenge.

Vorpal Tusks (Ex)

On a successful critical hit against a creature of up to one size category larger than itself, the razor boars's tusk slash attack severs the opponents head (if it has one) from its body. Though some creatures, such as golems and undead other than vampires, are not affected by the loss of their heads, most creatures die when their heads are cut off.

Trample (Ex)

Reflex DC 25 half. The save DC is Strength-based.

system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Listen checks and Spot checks.

system.description: As a standard action, the creature may choose to subtract 4 from its melee attack roll and deliver an awesome blow.
system.prerequisites: Str 25, Power Attack, Improved Bull Rush, size Large or larger
system.benefit: If the creature hits a Huge or smaller opponent with an awesome blow, the opponent must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC = damage dealt) or be knocked flying 10 feet in a direction of the attacker’s choice and fall prone.

system.description: You can remain conscious and act when below 0 hit points.
system.benefit:
When reduced to between -1 and -9 hit points, you automatically become stable. You don't have to roll d% to see if you lose 1 hit point each round.

When reduced to negative hit points, you may choose to act as if you were disabled, rather than dying. You must make this decision as soon as you are reduced to negative hit points (even if it isn't your turn). If you do not choose to act as if you were disabled, you immediately fall unconscious.

When using this feat, you can take either a single move or standard action each turn, but not both, and you cannot take a full round action. You can take a move action without further injuring yourself, but if you perform any standard action (or any other action deemed as strenuous, such as casting a quickened spell) you take 1 point of damage after completing the act. If you reach -10 hit points, you immediately die.

You gain a +4 bonus on the following checks and saves: Swim checks made to resist nonlethal damage from exhaustion; Constitution checks made to continue running; Constitution checks made to avoid nonlethal damage from a forced march; Constitution checks made to hold your breath; Constitution checks made to avoid nonlethal damage from starvation or thirst; Fortitude saves made to avoid nonlethal damage from hot or cold environments; and Fortitude saves made to resist damage from suffocation.

Also, you may sleep in light or medium armor without becoming fatigued.
system.special: A ranger automatically gains Endurance as a bonus feat at 3rd level. He need not select it.

system.description: You are skilled at pushing your opponents around.
system.benefit: When you perform a bull rush, you do not provoke an attack of opportunity from the defender. You also gain a +4 bonus on the opposed Strength check you make to push back the defender.
system.special: A fighter may select Improved Bull Rush as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You can make exceptionally powerful melee attacks.
system.benefit: On your action, before making attack rolls for a round, you may choose to subtract a number from all melee attack rolls and add the same number to all melee damage rolls. This number may not exceed your base attack bonus. The penalty on attacks and bonus on damage apply until your next turn.

system.description: Your Listen check is either made against a DC that reflects how quiet the noise is that you might hear, or it is opposed by the target's Move Silently check.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.
You are skilled at surviving in the wild and at following tracks.

What it does (SRD): The creature regains hit points each round at the rate given in the stat block (unless the rules say otherwise).

ThirdEra: There is no separate fast-healing numeric CGS row yet; track rounds at the table.

What it does (SRD): The creature can run over opponents at least two size categories smaller. Targets can attempt attacks of opportunity or Reflex saves to avoid (per stat block). Damage is typically based on the creature’s slam or listed trample damage.

ThirdEra: Use the printed DC and damage from the stat block during movement. This seed leaves Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty so you can copy the exact numbers from the SRD entry.

Vorpal tusks (Ex): On a confirmed critical vs a creature up to one size larger, severs the head (if any) — Fort/save interactions per SRD; many constructs and undead ignore decapitation.

Trample (Ex): Reflex DC 25 half; Strength-based.
